compatibility.title: Which Land Rover Models Use the 276DT?
compatibility.intro: The 276DT was Land Rover's first modern V6 diesel, introduced as part of the PSA/Ford-developed "Lion" engine family. It provided strong low-end torque and refined performance for the brand's heavy SUV lineup during the mid-2000s, serving as the volume diesel option before the introduction of the 3.0-litre successor.

failures.title: Land Rover 276DT Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Oil Pump Housing Failure - the defining failure
items.whatHappens: The plastic/composite oil pump housing is a critical weak point, particularly at the tensioner mount. When it cracks or fails under load, oil pressure drops rapidly, leading to immediate oil starvation and catastrophic bottom-end damage. A sudden drop in oil pressure or a cold-start knock is the primary early warning sign.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught extremely early, oil pump housing replacement is theoretically possible, but in practice most failures write off the engine due to rapid bearing and crankshaft damage. A full reconditioned or rebuilt unit is almost always required. [Read our full oil pump failure guide] .

items.title: Crankshaft & Bearing Failure
items.whatHappens: Crankshaft bearing failure is typically a secondary consequence of oil pump housing failure or oil starvation. Symptoms include deep knocking from the bottom end, low oil pressure, and eventually engine seizure.
items.repairVsReplace: Bottom-end rebuild is possible but labour-intensive and expensive (£5,500-£7,000). Most specialists recommend a full reconditioned unit instead, as the root cause (oil pump housing design) remains unaddressed in a partial repair.

items.title: Turbocharger & Snap Ring Issues
items.whatHappens: The twin-turbo setup is subject to wear at higher mileage, and the oil feed pipe snap rings can degrade, leading to oil leaks into the intake or onto the hot exhaust. Symptoms include excessive smoke, loss of power, and whining noises.
items.repairVsReplace: Turbo and oil pipe replacement is a standard repair and does not typically require a full engine replacement unless turbo debris has entered the oil system and caused bearing damage.

failures.goodYearsLine: The oil pump housing weakness is intrinsic to the original PSA/Ford Lion V6 architecture; while later production runs saw minor material revisions, the fundamental design risk remains present across all 276DT years and requires proactive inspection or replacement .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 276DT
variants.intro: The 276DT is Land Rover's designation for the PSA/Ford-developed 2.7L "Lion" V6 diesel. While it shares its core architecture with the later 3.0L variant and the Jaguar AJD-V6, confirming your exact code is critical because internal components, engine management, and ancillary brackets are not universally interchangeable. WHERE TO FIND THE CODE: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, usually visible near the bellhousing or on the cylinder head cover. It will also be explicitly listed on your V5C registration document under "Engine Code" or "Engine Capacity", and can be decoded directly from your 17-character VIN. COMMONLY CONFUSED CODES: - 306DT: The 3.0L successor introduced in 2009. While it shares the same basic V6 architecture, the 306DT has different bore dimensions, revised internals, and updated engine management, making it a non-straight swap. - Jaguar AJD-V6 2.7: Jaguar's designation for the exact same 2.7L engine. While mechanically identical, the engine loom, ECU, and mounting points differ between Land Rover and Jaguar applications - confirm fitment before purchasing a Jaguar-sourced unit. Why fitting the wrong revision matters: Attempting to swap a 3.0L long block into a 2.7L chassis without updating the ECU, loom, and fuel system will result in persistent fault codes and poor drivability. Similarly, a Jaguar-sourced AJD-V6 may require Land Rover-specific ECU mapping and loom adapters. CLOSING LINE: Not 100% sure? Enter your registration above - we'll confirm your exact 276DT fitment before any quotes are sent.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 276DT - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Land Rover 276DT engine is only advisable if it comes with comprehensive, documented proof that the oil pump housing has already been replaced with a revised design. Without this specific history, the risk of inheriting the same catastrophic oil pump failure is unacceptably high. This option is generally reserved for higher-value host vehicles where the budget is tight. Explore our vetted used Land Rover 276DT engine network.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned Land Rover 276DT engine is the most balanced and recommended choice for the majority of owners. A quality, specialist-led rebuild will systematically address the known weak points: an upgraded oil pump housing design, new turbochargers, revised timing chain set, and all critical gaskets and seals. This effectively resets the engine's reliability clock and is the most cost-effective way to secure long-term peace of mind. Compare reconditioned Land Rover 276DT engine options.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-mileage examples, vehicles that have suffered from oil starvation, or if the crankshaft shows measurable damage. An upgraded rebuild should include a revised oil pump housing design, new crankshaft bearings, reground crankshaft, and new turbochargers, ensuring the engine can reliably handle another 100,000+ miles. View rebuilt Land Rover 276DT engine specifications.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Buying through the EnginesMarket network means you can opt for a full supply and fit service, with the replacement engine installed by a Land Rover specialist and backed by a nationwide warranty. Learn more about supply and fit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The Land Rover 276DT is typically found in host vehicles (like the Discovery 3 L319 or Range Rover Sport L320) valued between £4,000 and £14,000 depending on condition and mileage. If your vehicle is at the lower end of this spectrum (e.g., an early Discovery 3 or high-mileage RR Sport valued under £7,000), a £5,000+ reconditioned Land Rover 276DT engine replacement may approach or exceed 60% of the car's total current market value. In these specific cases, we strongly advise evaluating the vehicle's scrap or part-exchange value before committing to a full Land Rover 276DT engine replacement.

items.question: What is the most common failure with the 276DT?
items.answer: The most common and severe failure is the oil pump housing cracking, particularly between 80,000 and 140,000 miles. This structural weakness leads to rapid oil starvation and catastrophic bottom-end damage. A sudden drop in oil pressure or a cold-start knock is the primary early warning sign.

items.question: Which Land Rover models use the 276DT engine?
items.answer: The 276DT was fitted to the Land Rover Discovery 3 (L319) and Range Rover Sport (L320) between 2004 and 2010. It served as Land Rover's first modern V6 diesel option, replacing older inline and BMW-sourced units. It is the exact same engine fitted to contemporary Jaguar models as the AJD-V6 2.7.
